stage1.impression: A view through a dark shopfront window down a long, low timber bar to a pair of glowing red speakers at the far end. The room behind the glass has believable depth, warmth and a record wall, but the frame is underexposed and mostly black steel. The speakers are tiny, read as red neon outlines rather than tinted acrylic, and compete with a second hot red patch on the record wall. The floor shows smeared reflections, and the bright flat slab at bottom right and the beige side room read as CG. A magazine would see a generic dark bar seen through a window, not a specific place: the shopfront's identity (the name, the lightbox) is not in the picture.

blocking_9: The shopfront's own identity must be legible: the name etched into the glass visible, and the frosted lightbox with the fogged dancing silhouette readable as such
Frame lum_median between 22 and 40, with the room behind the glass carrying the light and the steel holding texture
The Ember pair must read as tinted acrylic cabinets with light passing through them, not clipped red outlines (clip_pct under 1 on each speaker)
Red only on the speakers: no second saturated red patch on the record wall
No CG tells: no smeared denoiser streaks on the floor, no flat untextured bright plane at the sill or pavement
Composition: the speakers larger in frame, and the mullion off the record wall and counter
Delivered at 2400 x 1600 with 1:1 material detail (formwork grain, fir checks, steel patina)

defects.what: Left Ember speaker clips 8.4 % and reads as a red neon outline around a white disc, not as tinted cast acrylic; only about 25 px wide
Right Ember speaker clips 7.1 %, same reading as the left
Saturated red patch on the record wall (r 97, g 27, b 14), probably spill from the #FF5A3A disc; breaks the one-colour rule
Concrete floor shows smeared, streaky reflections typical of the denoiser; no aggregate or polish detail
Flat, bright, untextured beige slab at the sill or pavement (lum_median 123.5), the brightest large surface in the frame, reads as a CG plane
Side opening shows a beige wall, pink wainscot and a curtain lit brighter than the room (lum_median 60.4); it does not read as a frosted lightbox and no dancing silhouette is legible
No etched name visible anywhere on the glass (its emission is 0.0)
Window mullion cuts the frame vertically between the record wall and the counter
Blackened-steel pier is blotchy, mottled like a low-resolution texture, with no sharp edges or soft sheen; dark (lum_median 13.3)
Right edge is dead dark wall, 28 % crushed, with no information
Bare hot point light in the ceiling, a bright disc with no fixture
No street reflection or glass reflection at all, so the window reads as an open hole rather than glass

changes.problem: The shopfront's subject (the etched name and the frosted lightbox with the dancing silhouette) is invisible, so the picture loses its point and reads as a generic bar.

evidence.measured: No etched lettering visible anywhere on the glass; the card shows the window's etched name at 0.0; the side panel 530-640 x 140-310 shows a wall and curtain, not a frosted, evenly glowing panel

change.setting: the window's etched name (emission) and the lightbox / screens' images brightness
change.to: etched name 0.6 to 0.8 (edge-lit, warm 2700 K), so the letters catch light like frosted etching against the dark room; the lightbox's frosted panel 1.4 with frosted acrylic roughness raised so the silhouette is fogged and the panel glows evenly

changes.expected: The name reads as a pale frosted band on the glass at a glance; the lightbox reads as one even soft glow with a blurred figure inside.

changes.problem: The frame is too dark for a magazine night interior.
changes.expected: The frame's median rises into the low-to-mid 20s; the steel and the timber ceiling hold texture.

changes.problem: The Ember speakers clip and read as red neon outlines, not tinted acrylic with light passing through.

change.setting: lamps on each Ember speaker (4 x area) and the altar spots
change.from: 5.0 W/m2 at the target, 2900 K; altar 2 x 70 W
change.to: 2.0 W/m2 at the target; altar 2 x 90 W with the cone widened from 28 to 36 deg, so the cabinets are lit from outside and glow through the acrylic instead of blooming at the edges

changes.expected: Each speaker shows its tint as a body with a gradient across the acrylic, with no blown rim; median still 45 or more after c2.

changes.problem: A second saturated red patch on the record wall competes with the red speakers.

evidence.measured: r_median 97, g_median 27, b_median 14: as saturated as the speakers

change.setting: the disc behind the DJ station
change.from: emission 0.8 in #FF5A3A with a 60.0 W area lamp
change.to: emission 0.3 with a 15 W area lamp (or warm it toward #E0A070); raise the record wall's spots from 14 W to 20 W at 2600 K to keep the wall lit

changes.expected: The record wall turns warm brown and amber; the only saturated red left in the frame is on the speakers.

changes.problem: The speakers are about 25 px wide in a 720 px frame and the mullion splits the room; a third of the frame is dead pier and side wall.

evidence.measured: Pier and right wall lum_median 13.3 / 10.6, with 28 % crushed at the right edge; mullion at x 193-207

change.to: position [-2.6, 3.0, 1.5], lens 40 mm, target [17.0, 3.1, 1.3], keeping the shopfront's frame edges inside the picture and the etched name and lightbox in frame; place the mullion over the floor aisle, not over the counter or the record wall

changes.expected: The shopfront glass fills about 70 % of the width, the altar pair reads at about 1.4x their current size, and the dead wall shrinks to a thin dark border.

changes.problem: The floor reads as smeared CG: streaky reflections with no concrete detail.

evidence.measured: Streaks run along the view axis in the 2x crop; lum_range 89.5 with no fine texture

change.setting: the floor's polish and render settings
change.from: floor polish as now; samples 256, adaptive 0.02, denoise on
change.to: floor roughness raised by about 0.15 (honed, not polished) with aggregate and stain in the bump; samples 512, adaptive 0.01

changes.expected: The floor shows soft, broad pools under the Domes with visible aggregate and no directional smear.

changes.problem: The bright flat slab at the bottom right is the brightest large surface and reads as an untextured CG plane.

evidence.measured: lum_median 123.5, uniform (p5 16 is only the edge), r 156, g 118, b 79

change.to: 3 x point, 90 W, 3000 K, the nearest one moved so it rakes the pavement and the steel at a grazing angle; give the sill or pavement a worn concrete finish with roughness 0.8

changes.expected: The sill falls to a dim, textured kerb that does not pull the eye from the window.

changes.problem: The blackened steel pier is blotchy and soft and has no sheen, patina or crisp edges.

evidence.measured: lum_median 13.3, lum_range 30.9, mottled at 2x; edges soft

change.to: lower mottle contrast by half, roughness 0.45 with a brownish patina, edge wear on the arrises so the raking street light draws a thin highlight down each edge

changes.expected: The pier reads as near-black steel with a soft uneven sheen and one sharp highlighted edge.

out_of_scope.request: The Ember speakers' white batts and horn read as a white disc in a red frame at this size; a less outline-like tint would read better
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' shape, colour and parts are fixed; only their lighting is addressed (c3)

out_of_scope.request: The side room with the pink wainscot and curtain, if it is part of the room's design rather than the lightbox
out_of_scope.why: The room's layout and the shopfront are fixed; only its brightness can change. If it is meant to be the lightbox, its content must read as the fogged silhouette (c1)
